capture.final_message:
Treat the two conjuncts independently.

For the first, use the matroid basis-extension mechanism: choose a basis \(I\) of \(X\), then extend \(I\) along \(X\subseteq Y\subseteq E(M)\) to a basis \(J\) of \(Y\). This gives \(I\subseteq J\) with the required basis properties.

For the second, show that \(M_1\) and \(M_2\) have the same independent sets. If \(I\) is independent in \(M_1\), extend it to a base \(B\) of \(M_1\). By \(hM_1\), \(B\) is independent in \(M_2\), so hereditary closure gives that \(I\) is independent in \(M_2\). The converse follows symmetrically using \(hM_2\). Finally apply matroid extensionality using equality of ground sets and equality of independence predicates.

The ground-set hypothesis is essential: independence alone cannot detect additional loop elements outside the other matroid’s ground set.
